newsitem.title: USA: Freeze hurts Kansas wheat in key areas -- agronomist.
newsitem.headline: Freeze hurts Kansas wheat in key areas -- agronomist.

text.p: Four of the nine reporting districts in Kansas received moderate to severe damage to the wheat crop from the weekend freeze, said Jim Shroyer, extension agronomist at Kansas State University.

He noted the southwest, west-central, south-central and central districts were the worst hit. In 1996 they produced 142.9 million bushels, or 56 percent of the state's crop, according to the Kansas Agricultural Statistics Service.
"Southwest will be the worst. I think they have lost a considerable amount of tillers," he said, noting it was still too early to accurately estimate the extent of losses.
"I am hearing people wanting to go out and tear up their ground. That is the wrong thing to do. They should wait a couple of weeks," Shroyer said.
He said three more districts, the north-central, east-central and west-central, had slight damage. In 1996 they produced a combined 74.6 million bushels or 29 percent of the state's crop.
Two areas, the northwest and northeast, were seen least affected by the freeze.
Shroyer said dead tillers could be replaced by other tillers but the yield would be cut by at least 50 percent.
